messages:
Sam: CI started failing intermittently on Android instrumented tests that hit MockWebServer over HTTPS. Local device runs are flaky too. Anyone seen "mock" TLS EOF / handshake errors with Retrofit/OkHttp + cert pinning?

Sam: Example log: 
```
javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: Unexpected TLS packet: 0x15
Caused by: java.io.EOFException: SSL peer closed connection during handshake
```

Aisha: Are you using MockWebServer.useHttps(sslSocketFactory, false)? Also is cert pinning enabled in the test build or only prod?

Sam: useHttps yes. Pinning enabled in the test app build so we exercise it. Sometimes the test server sees repeated requests (duplicate POSTs). Suspect retries + non-repeatable body.

Diego: If an interceptor reads RequestBody.writeTo(Buffer) for logging and doesn't recreate the body, retries will send an exhausted body and weird errors when connection health check kicks in. Any interceptors that read bodies?

Sam: Yeah we have an analytics/logging interceptor that reads the body to compute a checksum and appends a header. Code looks like: 
```
Request req = chain.request();
if (req.body() != null) {
  Buffer b = new Buffer();
  req.body().writeTo(b);
  String payload = b.readUtf8(); // used for logging / checksum
}
return chain.proceed(req.newBuilder().header("x-checksum", checksum).build());
```

Aisha: That's the suspect. OkHttp may retry on connection failure and expects bodies to be repeatable. If you consume the body stream in the interceptor, it's gone for retries. That explains duplicate POSTs or partial writes seen by MockWebServer.

Diego: Also Android platform differences: some API levels have different socket timeouts and keepalive behavior, which makes stale-socket reuse more likely on certain devices/CI images. Combined with network flakiness you get EOF during TLS handshake.

Sam: Right. We saw it more on emulator images used by CI. What's the minimal fix? Buffering everywhere feels heavy.

Aisha: Two options: 1) Make a RepeatableRequestBody that buffers the bytes on creation (ok for small JSON). 2) Change interceptor to copy body bytes into a new RequestBody when you call chain.proceed. Example: 
```
byte[] bytes = bodyToBytes(req.body());
RequestBody replayable = RequestBody.create(mediaType, bytes);
Request newReq = req.newBuilder().method(req.method(), replayable).build();
return chain.proceed(newReq);
```

This keeps original behavior but makes retry safe.

Diego: If you want to keep retryOnConnectionFailure(true), prefer repeatable body. Alternatively set retryOnConnectionFailure(false) for tests but that hides real-world behavior.

Sam: Good call. We'll implement a small RepeatableRequestBody helper in the SDK tests and patch the interceptor to use it when body size < 64KB. Also will add MockWebServer.setProtocols(Arrays.asList(Protocol.HTTP_1_1)) and force TLSv1.2 in the test SSLContext to reduce protocol negotiation differences.

Aisha: Also add an assert in tests that MockWebServer.getRequestCount() == 1 after the call to catch duplicate POST regressions.

ci-bot: build #3044 (instrumentation) failed: flaky-network. Retrying... :gear:

Sam: I'll open a PR with the RepeatableRequestBody util and updated interceptor + a flaky repro androidTest that toggles pinning. Diego, can you review the helper?

Diego: Yep, will review. Also add a note to devex docs: "Do not consume request bodies in interceptors unless you recreate them". That's bitten other teams.

Sam: Will do. Thanks all. :pray:
